title: Statutory conditions on Schedule VI prescriptions by a retail collaborating pharmacist
rule_summary: Under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2(c)(5), a pharmacist in the retail setting who has a collaborative practice agreement with a supervising physician which specifically allows initial prescriptions for referred patients of the supervising physician may issue prescriptions for schedule VI controlled substances, as defined in clause 6 of section 3 of chapter 94C. Such prescriptions shall be for a patient diagnosis specified in the supervising physician's individual referral of that patient. A copy of the prescription shall be sent to the supervising physician within 24 hours.
exam_relevance: Tests the three statutory conditions on retail Schedule VI prescribing: an agreement that specifically allows initial prescriptions for referred patients, a diagnosis specified in the individual referral, and a copy to the supervising physician within 24 hours.

numeric_facts.fact: Time to send a copy of the Schedule VI prescription to the supervising physician
numeric_facts.conditions: prescription issued by a pharmacist in the retail setting under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2(c)(5)

common_confusions: An agreement that permits collaborative management in general does not satisfy the clause; it must specifically allow initial prescriptions for referred patients of the supervising physician.
The prescription must be for a patient diagnosis specified in the supervising physician's individual referral of that patient, not for any diagnosis the pharmacist identifies.
The statutory sentence on the 24-hour copy is written in the passive voice and does not itself name who sends it.
verification_notes: Read in the current text of M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2 on malegislature.gov on 2026-09-17.
